prompt.context_jp: 向かい合う大前春子の横顔を見つめる目に___、いつになく思い詰めた光があった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 向かい合う大前春子の横顔を見つめる目に___ 、いつになく思い詰めた光があった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the narrator's description of what existed in his eyes.

feedback.correct_en: は marks '目には' as the location/topic being described; the comment that follows ('a brooding light existed there') is the new information. This is a standard 'X には Y がある' topic frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly promote the eyes themselves to new-information subject, but the sentence already assumes the eyes and describes what was in them.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の目には涙があった。
contrast_examples.en: In his eyes, there were tears.
His eyes shone with tears. (eyes as new focus of the action)

prompt.context_jp: 賢ちゃんの言葉に、東海林___ぽかんと口を開けた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 賢ちゃんの言葉に、東海林___ ぽかんと口を開けた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best marks 東海林 as the topic here?

feedback.correct_en: 東海林 is already an established character; は frames him as the topic whose reaction we are now describing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal him as newly introduced or exhaustively singled out, which doesn't fit — we already know him. を is ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.en: It was Tōkaijin who was surprised. (identifying who)

prompt.context_jp: 二人の体温___、拍子抜けするほど平坦であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 二人の体温___ 、拍子抜けするほど平坦であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that fits the sentence commenting on their temperatures.

feedback.correct_en: は sets '二人の体温' as the topic and comments on it ('was surprisingly flat'). This is description-of-topic, not new info.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the temperatures as newly noticed information, but the narrative has just been describing the forehead-check scene — the temperature is the predictable topic.

contrast_examples.en: His temperature was normal. (comment on topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「プロポーズって 誰___ 誰に？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「プロポーズって 誰___ 誰に？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the wh-question 'who (proposed) to whom'?

feedback.correct_en: Wh-subjects like 誰 require が — they are by definition requesting new information to fill the slot.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰は is ungrammatical as a bare wh-question subject. を wouldn't fit the agent role of 'who proposed'.

prompt.context_jp: 今や 派遣なしに 会社___ 回らない
prompt.prompt_jp: 今や 派遣なしに 会社___ 回らない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the general statement about 'companies' not running without temps.

feedback.correct_en: This is a generic statement about companies as a topic/class. は fits the generalizing, thesis-statement tone of the narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark 'the company' as a specific new-info subject, which doesn't match this sweeping generalization.

prompt.context_jp: 隣に立つ大前春子だけ___、いつもと同じ 動じない横顔をしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隣に立つ大前春子だけ___ 、いつもと同じ 動じない横顔をしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after 'だけ' to express 'only Omae (and no one else)'?

feedback.correct_en: だけが gives exhaustive 'only X and nobody else' focus — Omae alone remained unshaken while everyone else was tense.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would imply 'at least Omae / Omae in contrast,' softer than the exhaustive 'only Omae' meaning the narration needs here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼だけは知らなかった。
contrast_examples.en: He alone didn't know (contrast with others).

prompt.context_jp: レジ横に必要なの___ ついで買いの和菓子では ありません
prompt.prompt_jp: レジ横に必要なの___ ついで買いの和菓子では ありません
prompt.prompt_en: Omae declares what is needed next to the register. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: 'The thing that's needed' (レジ横に必要なの) is set as the topic, and what follows corrects the misconception. は fits this 'X は Y ではない' structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify 'the needed thing' as new info, but Omae is pushing back on an existing claim — she's commenting on an already-raised referent.

contrast_examples.en: Courage is needed. (new focus on 勇気)

prompt.context_jp: この店のお金を出すの___ 私たちなんだぞ！
prompt.prompt_jp: この店のお金を出すの___ 私たちなんだぞ！
prompt.prompt_en: The investor claims who provides the money — which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The cleft structure 'Xのは Yだ' uses は to topicalize the relative clause and identify Y. 'The ones who pay = us.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が after のだ-style identification is possible in other framings, but here 'お金を出すのは私たち' is the natural cleft; のが would turn it into something like 'the fact of paying' as subject.

contrast_examples.en: The one who did it is him.

prompt.context_jp: 雇い止めという言葉の重み___、部屋全体を覆っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 雇い止めという言葉の重み___ 、部屋全体を覆っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The 'weight of the word' is newly introduced as the thing covering the room.

feedback.correct_en: The weight of the word is freshly introduced as the agent doing the covering — classic new-information が in narrative description.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize the weight as if already under discussion, but here it's introduced for the first time as the force filling the room.

prompt.context_jp: 派遣の思い付きと ＡＩ どちらを信用するか 君で___ 分かるだろう？
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣の思い付きと ＡＩ どちらを信用するか 君で___ 分かるだろう？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle gives the dismissive 'even you' nuance?

feedback.correct_en: '君でも' = 'even you' — the condescending tone Koyamada uses toward Satonaka. も adds the 'even' meaning.
feedback.incorrect_en: 君が would just mark subject neutrally; 君では would mean 'as for you' with no 'even' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 大前さん___ 勝てば アジフライを レジの横に置けるんだ
prompt.prompt_jp: 大前さん___ 勝てば アジフライを レジの横に置けるんだ
prompt.prompt_en: 'If Omae wins...' — which particle in the conditional clause?

feedback.correct_en: Subordinate conditional clauses (〜ば) typically use が to mark the subject within the clause, not the main-clause topic marker は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大前さんは勝てば… would weirdly try to topicalize Omae across the whole sentence; inside a conditional, が is standard.

contrast_examples.en: (awkward — は inside 〜ば is unnatural here)

prompt.context_jp: この一件が譲れぬ最後の砦であることを、彼だけ___ 知っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: この一件が譲れぬ最後の砦であることを、彼だけ___ 知っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: 'Only he knew' — which particle completes the exhaustive meaning?

feedback.correct_en: 彼だけが = 'he alone, and no one else' — exhaustive listing. The narrative stresses that Satonaka is the sole bearer of this knowledge.
feedback.incorrect_en: 彼だけは would soften to 'at least he / he in contrast,' losing the exclusive 'only he' punch.

contrast_examples.en: I (in contrast to others) won't go.

prompt.context_jp: でも 人間に___ たった一つだけ ＡＩにできないことがあります
prompt.prompt_jp: でも 人間に___ たった一つだけ ＡＩにできないことがあります
prompt.prompt_en: Omae contrasts humans with AI. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 人間には is contrastive-topic: 'as for humans (as opposed to AI), there's one thing...' This is classic は contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: 人間にが is ungrammatical. Even 人間が wouldn't capture the 'humans vs. AI' contrast Omae is building.

contrast_examples.en: As for me, I can't do it.
I'm the one who can't do it.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の辞書に “不可能”と“残業”の文字___ ない
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の辞書に “不可能”と“残業”の文字___ ない
prompt.prompt_en: 'The words "impossible" and "overtime" do not exist' — which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The existence negation 'XはYにない' with は carries the contrastive 'those particular words (unlike others) are not there' — the signature Napoleonic turn of phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report their absence as new info; the famous idiomatic structure uses は to highlight the contrast between these words and everything else in the dictionary.

contrast_examples.jp: 私の辞書に不可能の文字はない。
contrast_examples.en: The word 'impossible' is not in my dictionary. (contrastive flourish)

contrast_examples.jp: 辞書に間違いがあった。
contrast_examples.en: There was an error in the dictionary. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 大前君___ 速過ぎて ＡＩが追い付いてない
prompt.prompt_jp: 大前君___ 速過ぎて ＡＩが追い付いてない
prompt.prompt_en: Uno explains what's happening on the board. Which particle fits the 〜て clause?

feedback.correct_en: In a cause/explanation 〜て clause describing a surprising observation, が marks the subject as the new, salient cause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize Omae across the whole sentence, but Uno is reporting a sudden realization — が fits the 'she's too fast!' discovery tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降って、試合が中止になった。
contrast_examples.en: Rain fell, so the match was canceled.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は速くて、追いつけない。
contrast_examples.en: He is fast, so we can't catch him. (describing known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 失敗___ 人間だけにできる無駄
prompt.prompt_jp: 失敗___ 人間だけにできる無駄
prompt.prompt_en: Omae's thesis: 'Failure is the uselessness only humans can do.'

feedback.correct_en: 'XはYだ' definitional/thesis frame — Omae is defining what failure is. は topicalizes 'failure' and the predicate characterizes it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 失敗が would mark failure as newly introduced subject of some event, not as the topic being defined.

prompt.context_jp: ワゴンを押して現れたの___、なんと 東海林であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ワゴンを押して現れたの___ 、なんと 東海林であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this cleft revealing who appeared?

feedback.correct_en: The cleft 'XのはYだった' uses は: the known fact (someone appeared) is topicalized, and 東海林 is revealed as the surprising identity.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would turn the clause into a nominalized subject, not fitting this classic 'turns out it was ~' reveal.

contrast_examples.jp: 電話したのは彼だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who called was him.

prompt.context_jp: 「私は 大前さんを… 一緒に働いてくれる仲間を ___ます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私は 大前さんを… 一緒に働いてくれる仲間を ___ ます」
prompt.prompt_en: Satonaka declares what he does regarding his teammates, in opposition to trusting the AI.

feedback.correct_en: 信じる ('believe in / trust') is the dramatic counter to Koyamada's demand to trust the AI. Satonaka chooses human trust.
feedback.incorrect_en: 疑う means 'doubt' — opposite meaning. 頼る (rely) and 任せる (entrust) are close but don't fit the 'trust AI or trust people' binary set up in the scene.

contrast_examples.en: I leave it to my comrades.

prompt.context_jp: 大前が囲碁の対局で負けを認めた場面。「___」
prompt.prompt_en: The set phrase used to concede defeat in a game of Go/shogi.

feedback.correct_en: 参りました is the formal, traditional resignation phrase in Go and shogi — literally 'I'm beaten.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 負けました is grammatically fine ('I lost') but isn't the ritual phrase players actually use to concede at the board.

prompt.context_jp: 「あぁ… 混乱を ___ しまい 申し訳ありませんでした」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あぁ… 混乱を ___ しまい 申し訳ありませんでした」
prompt.prompt_en: Omae apologizes for causing confusion.

feedback.correct_en: 混乱を招く ('to invite/cause confusion') is the standard formal collocation, especially in business apologies.
feedback.incorrect_en: 混乱を作る/出す don't collocate naturally. 起こす is possible for 'cause' but 招く is the idiomatic business-apology verb here.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林に「壊れてないか？」と問われて、大前は「___ 運転ですが 何か？」と答えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ 運転ですが 何か？」
prompt.prompt_en: Omae's signature deadpan: 'I'm operating ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 平常運転 ('normal operations') is a set phrase borrowed from train/system announcements — a perfect robotic deadpan for Omae.
feedback.incorrect_en: 通常/正常 are related but 平常運転 is the fixed idiom that reads as her mechanical-sounding catchphrase.

contrast_examples.jp: ダイヤは平常運転です。
contrast_examples.en: Trains are running on normal schedule.

contrast_examples.jp: 正常に作動しています。

prompt.context_jp: 派遣社員たちが自分の将来を不安に思っている。「このまま ___ か…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「このまま___ か…」
prompt.prompt_en: The temp fears what will happen to their contract.

feedback.correct_en: 雇い止め = non-renewal of a fixed-term contract, a key labor-law term central to this drama's theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: 雇い入れ means 'hiring' (opposite). 引き止め means 'holding back / persuading to stay.' Neither fits the fear of contract termination.

contrast_examples.en: To have one's contract not renewed.

prompt.context_jp: 「そういうことかよ いや 激しく ___ な～！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「そういうことかよ いや 激しく ___ な～！」
prompt.prompt_en: Tōkaijin's reaction to Satonaka's 'propose-sounding-but-not' speech.

feedback.correct_en: 紛らわしい = 'confusing/misleading because it looks like something else' — exactly the chapter title's theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: 恥ずかしい (embarrassing), 羨ましい (enviable), 疑わしい (suspicious) don't capture the 'sounds like a proposal but isn't' confusion.

prompt.context_jp: 瞬く間にアジフライは___ように売れていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 瞬く間にアジフライは___ ように売れていった。
prompt.prompt_en: The fried mackerel sold extremely fast — which set expression?

feedback.correct_en: 飛ぶように売れる is the fixed idiom for 'selling like hotcakes' — literally 'selling as if flying.'
feedback.incorrect_en: The others are not conventional collocations with 売れる. Only 飛ぶように is the established idiom.

contrast_examples.jp: 商品が飛ぶように売れる。

prompt.context_jp: 「あなたは 会社に ___ ことを 考えたほうが いいんじゃないんですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あなたは 会社に ___ ことを 考えたほうが いいんじゃないんですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Omae tells Tōkaijin to focus on holding on to the company.

feedback.correct_en: しがみつく ('cling to desperately') captures the bluntly unsentimental image of a restructuring-target employee clinging to his job.
feedback.incorrect_en: The others don't fit 'cling to one's employer' and lack the slightly derogatory nuance Omae gives it.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林に「壊れてないか？」と心配された直後の、大前の返答として最も自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which response best captures Omae's trademark deadpan here?

choices.text: 平常運転ですが 何か？
いつも通りで、特に問題ありません。
大丈夫ですよ、心配しないで。

feedback.correct_en: Omae's signature pattern is '〜ですが 何か？' — a curt, slightly aggressive push-back that fits her mechanical persona.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other variants are grammatical and polite but lack the brusque challenge-tone the character is famous for.

contrast_examples.jp: アマチュア七段ですが 何か？

prompt.context_jp: 囲碁の勝負の最中、5時になって大前が去る場面。最も彼女らしい一言は？
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most like Omae at 5pm quitting time?

choices.text: もう5時になりましたので、申し訳ありませんが帰らせていただきます。
あ、5時だ！ 帰らなきゃ！

feedback.correct_en: The curt '5時なので失礼します' matches Omae's robotic, no-nonsense exits at exactly quitting time.
feedback.incorrect_en: The overly polite version sounds apologetic (unlike her), and the casual exclamation sounds too flustered for her character.

contrast_examples.jp: 定時なので失礼します。
contrast_examples.en: It's quitting time, so excuse me.

prompt.context_jp: アジフライを売り切った日の帰り際、大前が言うセリフとして最も物語の皮肉が効いているのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which line best delivers the ironic punchline of the chapter?

choices.text: 今日は 最高に 無駄な一日でした
今日は本当に充実した一日でした
今日はとても無駄な時間を過ごしました

feedback.correct_en: '最高に無駄な一日' flips her earlier speech — 'useless' is the very thing that makes humans human. The oxymoron '最高に + 無駄' is the point.
feedback.incorrect_en: '充実した' loses the 'useless' thread entirely; the third variant sounds like regret rather than the triumphant irony.

contrast_examples.jp: 最高に無駄な一日だった。
無駄な時間を過ごした。

prompt.context_jp: 宮部社長が二人の演説を受け流す時のセリフとして、最も冷ややかで社長らしいのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing best conveys the CEO's dismissive cool?

choices.text: どうも 熱弁 ありがとう だが それが何か？
熱い演説をどうもありがとう。でも、それが何だと言うのですか？
すごく熱い話だったね。でも意味わかんないよ。

feedback.correct_en: The clipped 'それが何か？' echoes Omae's own catchphrase back at them — a sharp, executive put-down loaded with irony.
feedback.incorrect_en: The verbose version loses the bite; the casual version doesn't match a CEO's register.

contrast_examples.jp: それが何だと言うのですか？
contrast_examples.en: What are you saying that means? (verbose)
